findings.F1: The book's gain comes almost entirely from the deepest runs, and the shallower runs add risk but no gain. Among the signal cases on folds B and C, runs whose fall exceeds 2.85 of the coin's 30-day daily swing gave a short-signed next-day move of +3.17 % (t 5.68, 56 cases). The other 161 cases gave -0.03 % (t -0.09). Weighted by the position held, the deep cases sum to +1.82 and the shallow ones to +0.05. Yet the shallow cases hold the worst single day (-15.3 % against -4.3 % for the deep ones). So the sizing, which caps typical and deep runs alike at -20, spreads the book's risk over cases that earn nothing. That fails Sharpe minus holding's (-0.10) and Calmar (0.23).
findings.F2: The grading the idea predicts is steep, and it lives in its top quarter. By depth quarter, the next-day short-signed move is -0.33 %, +0.44 %, -0.15 % and +2.95 % (t 5.96, 65 cases). By the 5-day return before the signal, the most fallen quarter gives +3.15 % (t 4.63) and the other three quarters give between -0.48 % and +0.16 %.
findings.F3: The depth on its own is not the effect; the up day that ends the run is. In falling markets, a deep run (depth over 2.85) still falling on the bar gives a next-day short-signed move of -1.66 % (t -2.67, 109 bars), a bounce. The same depth ended by an up day gives +3.74 % (t 7.26, 62 bars). So the deeper case belongs to the idea's own theory: more trapped holders sell at the first exit. It is not a separate effect.
findings.F4: The fall of a deep case keeps going beyond one day. Deep signal cases give a short-signed move of +4.16 % over 3 days (t 3.92) and +6.66 % over 5 days (t 4.74). On non-overlapping 5-day cells, the 5-day move is +6.89 % (t 4.74, 54 cases on 34 days), 36 times the 0.19 % cost of a trade. Shallow cases over 5 days give +0.49 % (t 0.59).
findings.F5: The book's deepest fall is a 216-day stretch from w7 to w9 that reaches -14.3 %. Over it the shallow cases lost: in w9, 38 shallow cases gave -0.85 % next day, while 7 deep cases gave +5.29 % (t 4.20). In w12, w13 and w17, shallow cases lost -0.94 %, -2.56 % and -0.84 % a day. In those three windows the deep cases were positive, or a single case.
findings.F6: The effect is not limited to calm markets, as the brief said. In falling markets, run-ending up days that the falling-calm book did not trade (outside the calm profile) gave a next-day short-signed move of +1.34 % (t 2.79, 89 cases). The traded ones gave +1.10 % (t 3.01, 164 cases). All falling-market bars that were not run-ending up days gave -0.07 % (t -0.52).

ideas.idea: In a falling, calm market, the first up day after a run of down days is followed by a fall in the coin's close over the next five days, and the deeper the run's fall against the coin's usual daily swing over the last 30 days, the larger that five-day fall.
ideas.consequence: A trader who shorts the relief day after a deep slide keeps the short for about a week, so the move is many times what the trade costs.
ideas.name: calm downtrend relief fade, week

ideas.idea: In a falling, calm market, the first up day after a run of down days is followed by a fall in the coin's close over the next day, and that fall grows ever more steeply as the run's fall deepens against the coin's usual daily swing over the last 30 days, so that almost all of it comes from the slides that are deepest against that swing.
ideas.consequence: A trader shorts relief days in proportion to how deep the slide was against the coin's usual swing, putting almost all the risk on the deepest slides, which carry the effect, and little on shallow ones, which only add losses.
ideas.name: deep slide relief fade

ideas.idea: In a falling market, the first up day after a run of down days is followed by a fall in the coin's close over the next day, and the deeper the run's fall against the coin's usual daily swing over the last 30 days, the larger that next-day fall.
ideas.consequence: A trader shorts the first relief day after a slide in any downtrend, agitated as well as calm, which gives the book more cases of the same effect.
ideas.name: downtrend relief fade, any swing
